title: Blocked/paged KV cache: GPU-aware paging and memory management design
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: implement a blocked/paged KV cache representation that is GPU-memory aware and integrates with continuous batching to reduce tail latency and overall GPU memory pressure. This ticket describes the data layout, eviction/pinning policies, asynchronous prefetch strategy, and interactions with CUDA/driver-level paging behavior.
comments: 2026-03-02 - Triage: Captured requirements from PM (low-latency chat workloads, high-concurrency embedding-like workloads). Decided to pursue block-based KV with 64-token page default and configurable page_size parameter.

2026-03-05 - Arch review: team agreed on block alignment by KV tensor row groups (layer-major blocks) to ensure coalesced loads. Trade-off: smaller blocks -> lower waste but more metadata and increased eviction churn; we settled on 64-token blocks as the baseline with runtime knob.

2026-03-08 - Prototype results: microbench harness shows 95th percentile latency improvement of ~18% for interactive chat traces when hot prefixes are pinned. Memory overhead measured at ~1.12x from metadata and staging buffers.
2026-03-10 - PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/5482 (blocked-kv-cache initial impl). Requesting ENG + infra review.
2026-03-12 - Design note updated: add async host->device prefetch with two-stream double-buffering and prefetch budget per GPU to avoid saturating PCIe on multi-tenant hosts.
2026-03-14 - In-progress: integrating with continuous batching scheduler; need to finalize metrics (page hit ratio, prefetch success rate) and expose knobs in console.
Next steps: complete code review, add e2e perf test against real chat traces, add dashboard widgets for page-level metrics, and prepare runtime-2.4 changelog entry.
acceptance_criteria: Blocked KV cache implements page/block metadata and supports configurable page_size (default 64 tokens).
Eviction policy: LRU at block granularity with hot pinning API for active prefixes (pin/unpin).
Asynchronous prefetch pipeline: CPU staging -> GPU async copy on dedicated transfer stream with overlap of compute and copy (double-buffering).
Fallback path: cold pages can be served from CPU memory with on-demand transfer; quantized storage allowed for cold blocks (int8/uint8) and dequantized on copy.
Integration tests that validate correctness across model checkpoint restore, multi-GPU sharding, and continuous-batching with mixed-length requests.
Perf targets: tail latency (95th) reduction >= 10% on sample chat workload and memory reduction of GPU-resident cold-state by >= 20% for long-context traces compared to current monolithic KV.
implementation_notes: Data layout: store KV as sequence of blocks referenced by (layer, head, block_index). Each block contains contiguous token KV rows for a fixed token range [b*page_size, (b+1)*page_size).

Metadata: per-block header with state={resident, staged, remote}, last_access_ts, size_bytes, and pin_count. Keep small inlined metadata in GPU for hot set; larger metadata on host. Metadata is O(#blocks) and is compressed with delta-encoding when shipped across processes.

Eviction: LRU on blocks. When memory pressure crosses threshold, evict coldest blocks to host memory or to quantized cold store. Eviction is cooperative with scheduler: do not evict blocks pinned by active batches.

Prefetch heuristics: predictive prefetch using prefix frequency and sequence-progress signals from the continuous-batcher. For batched requests with common prefixes, prefetch adjacent blocks ahead-of-time (lookahead of N blocks). Use adaptive budget: max_prefetch_bytes per GPU adjustable by tier.

Transfer mechanics: use cudaMemcpyAsync on a dedicated transfer stream and synchronize with compute stream via events. Use page-locked host staging buffers for DMA when transfers exceed a threshold. Implement double-buffering to ensure compute never stalls waiting for block transfer unless unavoidable.

Paged GPU memory behavior: avoid relying on OS/driver implicit UVM migration for predictable SLOs. We will support two modes: (1) Explicit-managed mode (default) where runtime controls all device residency and transfers; (2) UVM-compatible mode for experiments where cuMallocManaged is allowed (not recommended for production SLOs).

Quantized cold store: cold blocks can be stored quantized (4/8-bit) in host memory; on-prefetch we dequantize into GPU FP16/FP32 buffer. Dequantization and copy are overlapped; provide configurable decompression worker pool size.

Batching interaction: scheduler must communicate which blocks each batch will need (batch descriptor). The KV cache prefetcher subscribes and reserves pin_count for those blocks. Continuous batching should include block hints when enqueueing sequences.

Monitoring: emit metrics: kv_block_resident_count, kv_block_eviction_rate, kv_block_prefetch_success_rate, kv_block_pin_conflicts, kv_transfer_bytes/sec, and kv_block_access_latency histogram. Add logging for pathological eviction thrashing.
Safety: ensure crash-consistent metadata by checkpointing pin counts and resident map on graceful shutdown. During model upgrade, keep a compatibility shim for block index mapping.
